profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 49 (Lumen Technologies missing-address campaign): made several unsuccessful attempts to find a source for this legacy named Durham facility, including a broader area listing that explicitly did not include it, and declined to guess an address given none was found.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Lumen Technologies is the current legal successor to CenturyLink, which itself absorbed Level 3 Communications in a 2017 acquisition, with the CenturyLink brand renamed Lumen in 2020. Legacy Level 3 branding persists on some facilities and aggregator listings and is preserved in this registry per its no delete policy rather than overwritten. This specific row, Level 3 Communications, a legacy pre merger name preserved per this registrys no delete policy, in Durham, North Carolina, could not be matched to a specific address this session despite several attempts. Guessed direct URLs on Baxtel, datacenters.com, and datacentermap all failed with 404 or 403 errors, and a broader datacentermap area listing for the nearby Raleigh, North Carolina market, fetched fresh this session, explicitly showed no Lumen or Level 3 facility in Durham at all, listing only three Raleigh facilities instead. This sessions web search tool remained at its exhausted per session budget throughout, limiting research to direct page fetches on guessed URLs rather than fresh searches, which likely contributed to not finding a working source. No address was applied given no citable source was found.

reading.body:
This facility has no published power specification. The operator, Lumen Technologies, has not disclosed the megawatt capacity of this Durham location on any spec page this site has read. Without a power figure, the campus cannot be ranked among publishable AI infrastructure.

North Carolina has 19 mapped data center facilities, of which only 5 publish power figures totaling 50 MW. This facility ranks sixth by published capacity in the state, which means it publishes no capacity and falls outside the five published sites. The state's disclosed capacity is therefore 50 MW across those five facilities.

The address was recovered by reverse geocoding coordinates stored in OpenStreetMap under the facility's legacy Level 3 Communications name. The facility name reflects pre-2017 branding prior to Level 3's acquisition by CenturyLink, which later became Lumen Technologies. No certifications, specifications, or current operational details are published for this site.
